answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, as a result paying the cipher bond on all of them and exposing each to the ripple slash. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 13 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Because the ridge audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Collateral of 49 dollars is at risk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
